text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended at contract highs driven by steady fund buying through commission houses. October rallied $5.20 to close at an intraday and contract high of $329.90 a tonne, 20 cents above the previous contract high. The December contract finished at $324.00 a tonne, up $3.80.

Raw sugar futures in New York closed an actively traded session sharply higher and just under the new life-of-contract peaks reached across the board amid heavy fund buying. Today's gains were said to be driven by technical factors as the benchmark October contract triggered stops over 11.34 cents/lb and then at the previous contract highs of 11.40 cents/lb.

The October contract added 0.33 cent/lb to close at 11.59 cents/lb, having ranged from a contract high of 11.65 to 11.31 cents/lb. Second position March ended 0.27 cent firmer at 11.77 cents/lb after climbing to a lifetime high of 11.82 cents/lb. The rest of the board closed 0.21 to 0.25 cents firmer.

Prices can be expected to remain at current levels as the market has begun to act top heavy and gains were not reinforced by fundamental factors. Today's brisk activity was rather surprising as the market has been fluctuating within a rather tight trading range for the past several weeks and no fundamental news has emerged to support prices.

DENMARK - The weather in the fortnight ended July 20 was predominantly warm and sunny with temperatures above normal values. Precipitation levels since April 1 range between 147 and 183 mm compared to an average of 171-180 mm. Growth is reported to be very good. There were some local showers and humidity levels are rather high. Pest attacks are reported from some regions but their overall impact remains subdued. Crop prospects continue to be normal.

MAURITIUS - Sugar exports in April 1997 amounted to 6,533 tonnes, raw value, down from 7,606 tonnes in April 1996. This brought cumulative exports in the first 11 months of the 1996/97 campaign (June/April) up to 600,799 tonnes compared to 560,653 tonnes in 1995/96.

Total exports in 1995/96 amounted to 565,608 tonnes against 525,697 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries or destination in 1996/97 were the United Kingdom with 463,056 tonnes raws against 496,459 tonnes, Portugal with 83,104 tonnes, up from 19,080 tonnes and the USA with 25,502 tonnes compared to 3,213 tonnes.

In order to meet export obligations Mauritius is forced to import some tonnages and the total amount in June/April 1996/97 reached 30,876 tonnes compared to 32,778 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995/96 were 38,086 tonnes. Mauritius is importing exclusively from South Africa.

HONG KONG - Sugar imports in May 1997 amounted to 35,480 tonnes, raw value, up from 18,498 tonnes imported in May 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first five months of 1997 (January/May) up to 127,245 tonnes compared to 105,226 tonnes in the like period the previous year.

Total imports in 1996 reached 285,492 tonnes against 237,332 tonnes in 1995. Major countries of origin in January/May 1997 were South Korea with 69,772 tonnes whites against 47,806 tonnes, the United Kingdom with 16,404 tonnes, up from 10,696 tonnes and China with 17,001 tonnes raws against 3,977 tonnes.

Sugar exports in May 1997 amounted to 13,200 tonnes, which brought cumulative exports in January/May 1997 up to 47,760 tonnes compared to 35,558 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1996 reached 80,533 tonnes against 67,970 tonnes in 1995. The major country of destination in January/May 1997 was China with 40,540 tonnes whites against 23,235 tonnes.

State-owned Bangladesh Sugar and Food industries Corp said it bought 25,000 tonnes of white sugar at $339.70 per tonne, c&f, for shipment during September 2-9. Corporation officials said Kerry Foodstuffs of Britain won the deal in a bidding on July 20. The first cargo of 12,500 tonnes should reach Bangladesh by September 2 and the rest by September 9, it was added. The Corporation official said his country had bought a total of 140,000 tonnes of sugar for calendar year 1997 and that its importing programme was now completed. The next bidding is expected early next year, he added.
